newsitem.title: MOZAMBIQUE: Mandela awards medal to late Mozambican leader.
newsitem.headline: Mandela awards medal to late Mozambican leader.

text.p: President Nelson Mandela honoured Mozambique's former leader Samora Machel posthumously on Saturday, presenting South Africa's highest award for foreign citizens to Machel's widow Graca.
Mandela gave the Order of Good Hope Class One, Grand Cross Gold, to Graca Machel, who recently acknowledged that she and the South African president have "an amorous relationship".
He presented the award at a ceremony held in Maputo's Independence Square to mark the 10th anniversary of Machel's death in a mysterious air crash in South Africa.

Two kings, two presidents, representatives of many governments and tens of thousands of Mozambicans took part in the ceremony at the square where Machel proclaimed independence for Mozambique in 1975.
"It is a great honour and a privilege to join you here in Maputo to pay homage to a Mozambican patriot whom we in South Africa can also claim as our own," Mandela said.
"By shedding his blood on our soil Samora Machel left a part of himself with us."
The Mozambican authorities have frequently expressed the suspicion that the plane was lured off course by a false radio beacon set up by the former apartheid regime.
The plane was headed for Maputo airport but instead crashed into a mountain at Mbuzini in South Africa.
"He was a passionate supporter of our cause. The tragedy that befell us 10 years ago still defies description," Mandela said.
"We mourn a soldier who trained the fighters of Umkhonto we Sizwe (the armed wing of Mandela's African National Congress) and we mourn an intellectual who inspired our youth."

Graca Machel, who has said she will not marry Mandela despite her love for him, said the medal belonged to the Mozambican people and particularly the nation's children "who Samora described as the flowers that never wither".

At the end of her speech, Graca Machel led the crowd in one of the songs which her late husband used at mass rallies to whip up support for his government's campaign against white minority regimes in Rhodesia (now Zimbabwe) and South Africa.

Among the leaders who made speeches at Saturday's ceremony were Mandela, King Mswati of Swaziland, King Letsie of Lesotho, President Jose Eduardo dos Santos of Angola and President Ketumile Masire of Botswana.
